evals.prompt: Convert tests/pdfs/crowd.pdf to Markdown. This is an academic paper with two-column layout. Preserve section headings, abstract, figures, and any benchmark tables. Output the Markdown file alongside an images/ folder for extracted figures.
evals.expected_output: A Markdown file that reconstructs the two-column academic paper into single-column reading order. Section headings (Abstract, Introduction, Related Work, Method, Experiments, Conclusion) use # / ## syntax. Figures are referenced with ![](images/...) at their logical positions. Any multi-column fidelity issues are flagged with HTML comments.
expectations: Two-column layout is merged into single-column reading order — text does not interleave between columns
Standard academic sections (Abstract, Introduction, Related Work, etc.) are promoted to ## headings
Paper title appears as a # heading at the top
Author names and affiliations are preserved as body text, NOT promoted to headings
Figure captions remain as body text below the image reference, not promoted to headings
Any benchmark/results tables use Markdown pipe syntax with header rows
Images/figures are extracted to images/ directory and referenced with ![](images/...) syntax
Equations or mathematical notation are preserved as best as possible (LaTeX or plain text)
Multi-column layout warnings are inserted as <!-- WARNING: multi-column layout --> comments
No content from abstract, body, or references is silently dropped

evals.prompt: Extract all figures and diagrams from tests/pdfs/crowd.pdf into an images/ folder. Produce a Markdown file that references each figure at its correct position in the paper's reading order. This paper likely has crowd density maps, architecture diagrams, and result visualizations.
evals.expected_output: An images/ directory with extracted figures as PNG files, and a Markdown file referencing each figure inline. Figure numbering should match the paper's original Figure N labels. Vector graphics that cannot be rasterized get HTML comment warnings.
expectations: All raster figures are saved to images/ as PNG files
Each figure is referenced with ![Figure N](images/...) at its logical document position
Figure captions are preserved as text below the image reference
Architecture diagrams or flowcharts are extracted if raster; flagged with <!-- WARNING --> if vector-only
Result visualization plots (density maps, heatmaps) are captured
Figures are NOT duplicated — each appears once at its logical position
Image filenames are descriptive or follow page_img pattern

evals.prompt: Convert tests/pdfs/ds987-k26-som.pdf to Markdown. Preserve the document structure — especially section headings, lists, and paragraphs. Output the Markdown file alongside an images/ folder for any extracted figures.
evals.expected_output: A Markdown file that mirrors the original PDF structure with correct heading hierarchy using # syntax, readable paragraphs, and image references pointing to images/ directory. Section headings are promoted from bold/large-font PDF text to proper Markdown heading syntax. Any layout limitations are flagged with HTML comment warnings.
expectations: Real section headings in the PDF are promoted to Markdown heading syntax (#, ##, ###) — not left as bold text or unstyled lines
Heading hierarchy reflects the logical document outline (e.g., chapter > section > subsection)
Long prose lines (>80 chars or full sentences) are NOT promoted to headings even if bold/large in the PDF
Cross-reference sentences (e.g., 'See Section 4.2') are NOT promoted to headings
Legal or disclaimer prose is NOT promoted to headings even when bold or large-font
Every # line in the output is a short, genuine structural heading — no false positives
Images are extracted to images/ and referenced with ![alt](images/...) syntax
Multi-column fidelity warnings are inserted as HTML comments
No content from the PDF is silently dropped

evals.prompt: I need the tables from tests/pdfs/ds987-k26-som.pdf converted to proper Markdown tables with column alignment. The PDF contains tables with merged and spanning cells. Focus on getting the tabular data right — I'll use it in a downstream data pipeline.
evals.expected_output: Markdown output where every table in the PDF is rendered as a pipe-delimited Markdown table with a header row and separator row. Merged or spanning cells are normalized so every row has equal column count, with a warning comment above the affected table.
expectations: Tables are rendered using Markdown pipe syntax (| col1 | col2 |) with header separator rows
Merged or spanning cells are normalized: spanned values repeated or empty cells inserted for equal column count
A <!-- WARNING: merged/spanning cells --> comment appears above each affected table
Sparse spanning rows (sub-headers or note rows) are preserved — not collapsed or dropped
Continuation content in spanning rows appears in the correct column
Post-conversion table verification is performed
If initial conversion misses tables, a pdfplumber fallback is attempted
Section headings above tables use # syntax, not bold or plain text
Approximately 49 tables should be extracted (known from baseline)

evals.prompt: Extract all images and diagrams from tests/pdfs/ds987-k26-som.pdf into an images/ folder, and give me a Markdown file that references each image in the correct reading order. Warn me about any vector diagrams that can't be extracted as raster images.
evals.expected_output: An images/ directory containing extracted raster images as PNG files, and a Markdown file that references each image inline at the correct document position. Vector graphics that cannot be rasterized are flagged with HTML comment warnings.

Each image is referenced with ![](images/...) at its correct position

expectations: Specification section headings use # / ## / ### hierarchy matching the document outline
Protocol state tables preserve all states and transitions

Register map tables preserve bit field definitions with correct widths and addresses
Spanning header cells (grouping parameters by category) are normalized

<!-- WARNING --> comments on tables with complex merged cells

evals.prompt: Focus specifically on the tables in tests/pdfs/UM10204.pdf that have merged or spanning cells. Hardware specification documents often group parameters under spanning category headers (e.g., 'AC Electrical Characteristics' spanning multiple sub-parameter rows). expectations: Every table row has equal column count — no ragged rows
Full-width spanning category headers are either: (a) extracted as ## sub-headings above the table, or (b) included as a full-span row with empty padding cells
Parameter grouping rows (e.g., 'Standard-mode', 'Fast-mode') are preserved, not collapsed
Min/typ/max columns aligned correctly — values in the right column
Condition columns (e.g., 'at VDD = 3.3V') are preserved
Footnote markers (*, †, 1, 2) in table cells are preserved
<!-- WARNING: merged/spanning cells --> appears above each normalized table
